From: security@alpenglow.health

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: SIG questionnaire — ephemeral session logs & forensic snapshot question

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this. We're working through Redwood-related items on the SIG/CAIQ for our security review. A couple of specific questions about ephemeral session events (the short-lived conversational/session traces produced by the hosted API):

- What is Redwood's default retention window for ephemeral session events and derived telemetry for hosted customers? Is there any difference between streaming generation (chunked responses) and non-streaming calls?
- For compliance/forensics purposes, can Redwood produce a 7-day forensic snapshot for a single tenant (tenant-id provided) on request? If yes, please describe the preservation workflow (who runs it, what artifacts are produced, expected SLA to deliver the snapshot).
- Does Redwood perform any irreversible deletion (secure wipe) for ephemeral traces before the default retention window ends (e.g., background trimming vs. immediate purge on customer request)?
- We need evidence for SIG control DI-2. Specifically: a short attestation or runbook and sample artifact names we can expect (logs, indexes, KV-cache dumps, timestamps).

I've attached our current SIG questionnaire pages that reference these items (SIG-questions-v2.pdf). If it's easier, we're fine with a quick call to walk through. Thanks — we need to include your answers with our vendor pack by next Friday.

Best,
Hannah Lee (Security Lead)
Alpenglow Health
security@alpenglow.health

Attachment: SIG-questions-v2.pdf (PDF, 312KB)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: security@alpenglow.health
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire — ephemeral session logs & forensic snapshot question

Hannah — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by a proposed next step and what we can deliver as artifacts.

Short answers:
- Default retention (hosted API): ephemeral session events and derived telemetry are retained for 30 days by default. Streaming vs non-streaming does not change retention policy; both generate the same session-event records.
- Ad-hoc 7-day forensic snapshots: yes — we can produce a tenant-scoped snapshot that contains the last N days of session events (we can limit to a 7-day window). For hosted customers this is an ad-hoc export run by our forensics team; delivery SLA is typically 3 business days after request and verification (unless you require a signed SOW and longer timelines).
- Deletion semantics: we do not perform irreversible secure-wipe actions automatically before the retention window; deletions are time-based trimming. We support customer-initiated holds where we pause scheduled truncation for the specified tenant.
- Artifacts: we can provide compressed event exports (JSONL), a session-index CSV with timestamps and request IDs, and a manifest describing the export parameters. We will include checksums for integrity.

What we will provide for your SIG pack (we can attach): retention-matrix.pdf (high-level table), a short attestation template, and a draft runbook for the snapshot process.

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether you need the 7-day snapshot to be ad-hoc (on-demand) or a rolling 7-day window maintained continuously. If ad-hoc, confirm tenant-id and authorized signer for receiving artifacts.
2) If you need an attestation signed, let us know and we will route to Legal for a brief statement of capabilities and limitations.
3) If helpful, let's schedule a 30-minute call Wednesday or Thursday to walk through the artifacts.

I've looped in Marissa (CS) to coordinate tenant details and Jonas (Compliance) for any attestation requirements.

Thanks,
--
Sooj in Lee
Senior Security Program Manager | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0168

Sooj in / Marissa / Jonas — thanks for the quick response and for the proposed artifacts. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We require ad-hoc 7-day forensic snapshots (not a continuous rolling window). Alpenglow will request these on a case-by-case basis (typically triggered by an incident or regulatory inquiry).
- For each request we will provide the tenant-id, an incident reference number, and the authorized recipient (security@alpenglow.health or a designated vendor).
- We also require a one-time attestation that Redwood can produce a tenant-scoped export containing the full session-event payloads (JSONL), associated session index, and manifest within 3 business days of an authenticated request. This attestation can be limited to hosted customers with the stated SLA; we understand Dedicated/Private will be handled per contract.

Next steps: please send the retention-matrix.pdf, the draft runbook, and the attestation template. We will review and (likely) ask Legal to include an addendum in our vendor paperwork. We also plan to send a short SOW via DocuSign to cover any additional work.
